clue.text: A Catholic hospital defended by some in lawless state

indicators.note: a thing defended by others is surrounded by them, so the following word wraps the earlier pieces

parts.note: some, as in 'have you got any', means any
RC is the standard abbreviation for Roman Catholic
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A Catholic hospital, protected by a few loyal people, stands amid a country gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defended by' means the word for 'some' surrounds the other pieces; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a condition with no government or law, exactly a lawless state.

clue.text: Unusual socialist accompanied by people in hunt

parts.note: socialists are on the political left
the riders following a foxhunt are collectively called the field

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist turns up oddly among the riders of a foxhunt.
explanation.walkthrough: In British foxhunting the FIELD is the body of mounted followers; 'accompanied by' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left-field is unconventional or out of the ordinary, an idiom from baseball.

clue.text: Some doffed or adjusted headwear

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gentleman's hat is either raised politely or set straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in 'doffed' and ends in 'or', with 'Some' signalling only part of the text is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown, a type of headwear.

clue.text: Limit European policy connected with a built-up area

parts.note: CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Union
a city is a large built-up area

explanation.surface: An EU farming rule is tied to the boundaries of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the maximum amount something can hold, its upper limit.

clue.text: Indicate loft in untidy yard in secret state

indicators.note: untidy suggests things left in a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yard as a unit of length

explanation.surface: A note directs someone to a loft within a messy back yard, all hush-hush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' scrambles INDICATE, LOFT and IN together; Y for yard closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidentiality is the condition of being kept private, a state of secrecy.

clue.text: Picture left by artist with charisma

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
IT means sex appeal or charisma, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A painting left behind by a magnetic painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' merely links; IT for appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted or drawn picture of a person.

clue.text: Top research briefly featuring in court

indicators.note: a thing featuring in another appears inside it, so the short form goes within

parts.note: RES is the short form of research

explanation.surface: Short bits of research appear in a legal hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crest is the top of a hill or wave, its highest point.

clue.text: Attendants on queen in coach

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another stands above it

parts.note: a train is a retinue of attendants following a dignitary
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Courtiers wait on Her Majesty inside her carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer coaches athletes, so the verb-made noun coach is a synonym.

clue.text: Girl facing river in additional room?

indicators.note: the girl faces the river, so her name comes first with it straight after

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A girl stands looking out at a river from her spare room.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building or room added on, so an additional room.

clue.text: Crackpot engraves weapon

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, telling us the letters are rearranged madly

explanation.surface: An eccentric carves a weapon's design.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical agent used as a weapon of war.

clue.text: Estate, maybe, that's ruined in no time, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound, not spelling

parts.note: right off means immediately, in no time at all

explanation.surface: A ruined property sells in a flash, so rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is a British estate car (a station wagon); one written off in a crash is beyond repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-off is a vehicle damaged beyond economic repair, as an estate car may be.

clue.text: Corpulent leader of team must be kept in shape

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the leading letter goes within the shape

parts.note: round is a shape

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fat captain is told to stay in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means plump and round in body, a synonym for corpulent.

clue.text: Greet in sun daughter in Asian country

indicators.note: the greeting goes in the sun word, placed inside it

parts.note: to sun yourself is to tan
hail means greet

explanation.surface: A father welcomes his daughter, basking in the sun of an Asian holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand is a kingdom in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Engish spymaster is perhaps protecting Republican agent

parts.note: the printed misspelling of English, abbreviated E
M is the head of the secret service in the Bond stories

indicators.note: a protector surrounds what it shields, so this piece wraps the other

parts.note: say means perhaps or for example

explanation.surface: Britain's spy chief is perhaps shielding an American agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engish' is a typo for English as published.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is someone sent on a mission, an agent representing another.

clue.text: A last tune played in Muslim territory

indicators.note: a tune played is rendered anew, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A final melody is performed in an Islamic land.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate is a country ruled by a sultan, typically a Muslim ruler.

clue.text: Free information definitely arising about origin of opera

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word wraps the next letter
arising means coming up, and in a down answer the word is read upwards

parts.note: sure means definitely

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Free details certainly emerge about the beginnings of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous means free in giving, liberal with money or time.

clue.text: Senior academic largely hated scruffy tie

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a dean is a senior university figure

indicators.note: scruffy means messy, so these letters are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A college head mostly loathed the shabby necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race that ends in a tie between competitors.

clue.text: Activity promoting unrest initially ignored becoming issue

indicators.note: the opening letter is ignored, so it is dropped from the front

parts.note: sedition is conduct inciting rebellion against authority

explanation.surface: Stirring up rebellion was overlooked at first, becoming a matter of debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is an issue of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Favoured condition entered by European is provisional

parts.note: in means in favour, popular

indicators.note: a thing entered by another has it inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a term is a condition of an agreement
I is the international code for Italy, so an Italian, a European

explanation.surface: A popular clause, accepted by a European, is only temporary.
explanation.walkthrough: I comes from IVR codes for Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means temporary, in place until something permanent arrives.

clue.text: Educated woman among Irish conservationists, one proving troublesome?

indicators.note: a thing among others sits in their middle, so the name goes between

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation body
Rita is the hairdresser in Willy Russell's play Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A learned lady among Irish heritage workers is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic British houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything that causes annoyance or trouble.

clue.text: Use abusive language against English organ that's taken up

indicators.note: in a down answer taken up means read from the bottom, reversing the run

parts.note: the liver is an organ

explanation.surface: Insulting an English organ that has been hoisted aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: To revile is to criticise abusively, verbally attacking someone.

clue.text: Paper beginning to tackle point in dispute

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an issue is a matter under debate

explanation.surface: A paper starts to address a contested point.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, as in tissue paper.

clue.text: Stop trader's outlet?

definitions.meaning: to bring to a halt or cease
a market stand from which goods are sold

explanation.definitionFit: Stall means to halt, and a stall is a booth where a trader sells goods.

clue.text: One selling in US city source of perfume

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a vender is a seller, a variant of vendor

explanation.surface: A salesperson in Los Angeles deals in fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links; LA comes first, then VENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender flowers yield an oil used widely in perfumes.

clue.text: European capital associated with a lot of drink and food from Italy

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

indicators.note: a lot of means most of, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: tonic is a mixer drink

explanation.surface: A Baltic city linked with heavy drinking and Italian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a ribbed tube-shaped pasta from Italy.

clue.text: Vent one's feelings in journey for Franglais speakers?

definitions.meaning: French 'le' with English 'trip' makes a mixed-language phrase for a journey

explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is to express feelings freely; split as French le plus English trip it means a journey.

clue.text: View certainly backed in British island

parts.note: an angle is a viewpoint

indicators.note: backed means moved back, so the word is written in reverse

parts.note: yes means certainly

explanation.surface: A viewpoint confirmed on a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns YES into SEY; Anglesey is an island off north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is an island off northwest Wales, in Britain.
